item.title: Why Jung Cheong-rae Won't Stop Even After Losing the 'Myeong-Cheong Battle' (‘명청 대전’ 지고도 정청래가 멈추지 않는 이유)
item.description:
Why Jung Cheong-rae Won't Stop Even After Losing the 'Myeong-Cheong Battle' (‘명청 대전’ 지고도 정청래가 멈추지 않는 이유)

With Kim Min-seok elected as party leader at the Democratic Party's national convention, a new 'Myeong-Seok system' combining President Lee Jae-myung and Representative Kim has been launched. Jung Cheong-rae, the former leader who had competed against Representative Kim in the 'Myeong-Cheong battle,' is now out of power. The era of the 'Myeong-Cheong conflict' is over, and the 'Myeong-Seok solidarity' and 'Pro-Myung one-team' system is now in full operation. <<> In the past, candidates who lost a party convention typically kept quiet and entered a period of self-restraint. But former leader Jung Cheong-rae shows no sign of lowering his voice or bowing his head. Rather, he appears determined to say what he has to say and expand his political influence. <<> Immediately after the convention, Jung said, "Jung Cheong-rae lost, but his supporters won," and "Kim Min-seok won, but his arguments lost." He also said, "I lost in numbers, but I didn't lose my passion and values." He added, "Many people say I should leave the party because I didn't become party leader, but you absolutely must not do that. If you all leave the party, how can I survive all alone? Stay with me to the end and protect me." <<> To the pro-Jung supreme council members, he also said, "I trust you will play a 'major role' under Representative Kim Min-seok's system." Although he lost this primary, he remains politically viable, so he urged them to continue helping and supporting him. This reveals his intent to keep up the 'Jung Cheong-rae struggle' by playing the role of an opposition within the ruling party even under the Kim Min-seok system. <<> Why does Jung refuse to stop his fighting mode even after losing the 'Myeong-Cheong battle'? Does he believe there's a chance of winning an internal power struggle within the ruling party, given that the president's power is at its most formidable in the 'second year of his term' and the pro-Myung faction has regained control of the party? <<> The biggest reason Jung wants to raise the banner of independent factionalization after his convention defeat is reportedly 'resentment.' Jung has reportedly confided to those around him, "I couldn't speak out, and I've endured so much injustice." He claims he never intended to defy or disobey the president's wishes, yet the pro-Myung leadership treated him like a traitor or renegade. So now, he reportedly feels a strong urge to speak his mind freely—things he couldn't say as party leader. <<> The second reason is his confidence that while he lost the vote among paid party members in the Honam region, he won in the general public opinion poll. In the public opinion survey released on convention day, Jung edged out Representative Kim by 1.4 percentage points. However, that figure includes preference votes (second-choice votes for candidate Song Young-gil). In a simple head-to-head support race between just Jung Cheong-rae and Kim Min-seok, Jung was reportedly ahead by about 4–5 percentage points. <<> Jung said, "Before adding the first-round second-choice votes from the public opinion poll, I think I was winning by about 5 percentage points." In other words, he lost among paid party members but won among the general public. This is interpreted as an emphasis on 'public sentiment is on my side.' Even in paid party member votes outside Honam—in the capital region and other areas—the vote gap between Kim and Jung was negligible. <<> He is actively touting that while Honam votes swung to Representative Kim because of the president's '80 trillion won Honam semiconductor mega-cluster investment plan,' he was never behind in party sentiment in the capital region, Yeongnam, or Chungcheong, nor in general public opinion. He appears to have concluded that he can survive as an independent force even under the Kim Min-seok system. <<> The third reason is the uncertain future of the 'Myeong-Seok system.' Although Representative Kim won the primary thanks to the president's full-throated support and Honam public backing, a rosy future is not guaranteed. Nearly half of the party members did not support Representative Kim. If he makes even a small mistake, the anti-Kim forces within the party could grow. <<> There are also many risk factors: real estate policy, the issue of dropping prosecutorial appeals, the constitutional amendment controversy, prosecutorial reform, and conflict with the judiciary. If any one of these goes wrong, the approval ratings of both the president and Representative Kim could fall together. For Representative Kim to resolve difficult issues and break through the political impasse, he will also need internal cooperation and support from the pro-Jung faction. <<> For Jung, there is room to grow his presence by speaking out on various issues. He could also elevate his position as an opposition within the ruling party. Although he lost to the 'Myeong-Seok alliance' in the primary, he believes the path to a comeback remains open if he maintains his political influence. Conversely, for the president and Representative Kim, winning the primary has left a bitter aftertaste. <<> On the first day of the Kim Min-seok system, the mood between the party and the presidential office was better than ever. The presidential office's political affairs team mobilized from early morning to deliver a congratulatory flower basket to Representative Kim. Usually, the senior presidential secretary for political affairs delivers such baskets, but on this day, Chief of Staff Kang Hun-sik, Senior Political Affairs Secretary Hong Ik-pyo, and Political Affairs Secretary Jung Eul-ho all came, and they even embraced Representative Kim. <<> The new leadership's first schedule is typically a visit to the National Cemetery. But on this day, the first item was a meeting between the party and the presidential office. This too is unusual. It's a scene that shows how much the presidential office welcomes Representative Kim's election. Both sides emphasized being 'one team without walls.' This speaks to how severe the conflict and breakdown in communication had been during Jung Cheong-rae's tenure. <<> Inside the presidential office, some reportedly said, "Representative Kim's election is President Lee's victory." This shows how much effort and anxiety the president invested in getting Kim elected. On the 19th, the president invited the three party leader candidates to the presidential office for dinner. He urged them to unite as one team centered on the new leadership. With a party-government meeting on real estate held that day, the first high-level party-government-presidential office meeting takes place on the 23rd. The 'Myeong-Seok one-team system' is now in full operation. <<> Some in the presidential office and the pro-Myung camp are also sensing a somewhat uneasy mood about the primary results. The presidential office and pro-Myung forces had expected a landslide victory. There was the announcement of the 800 trillion won Honam semiconductor investment and the president's order for a 'blitzkrieg.' Yet the capital region was a tight race, and they actually lost in the public opinion poll. They went all-in at the government level but failed to achieve a crushing victory. <<> There are three things the pro-Myung leadership finds particularly unsettling. First, excluding the preference votes in the poll, Representative Kim trailed Jung by about 4–5 percentage points. Jung also emphasized this—that he won among general public sentiment. <<> In the supreme council member race, pro-Jung candidates took first, second, and third place in the public opinion polls. Not only did all three who ran get elected, but they outnumbered the elected pro-Myung supreme council members (two). This gives them a numerical base in the supreme council to check Representative Kim. <<> Third, Kim Yong, the president's closest aide, lost despite other candidates withdrawing and publicly endorsing him. Although the pro-Myung camp supported him wholeheartedly, Kim's defeat came as a surprise. Kim finished last in the polls. This means that sentiment toward the president and his pro-Myung inner circle is worse than expected. <<> Although the Jung Cheong-rae system was toppled, the tasks facing the 'Myeong-Seok system' are piling up. The most urgent is real estate. There is strong criticism of the government's announced tax reform and supply measures for real estate. Representative Kim said he would 'fine-tune taxes' and 'devise supply measures,' but these are not easy tasks. <<> On the issues of constitutional amendment for presidential re-election or a two-term system, and dropping prosecutorial appeals, there is no disagreement between the party and the presidential office, but the opposition is pushing back and public opinion is not favorable. Party integration is even harder. In key party positions such as secretary-general and policy committee chair, most appointments have gone to pro-Myung figures. With three pro-Jung members on the supreme council, balanced appointments are difficult for now. <<> The biggest question is whether Jung and the pro-Jung camp will cooperate with the Kim Min-seok system. In this regard, pro-Jung figures are saying, "We will cooperate for the success of the Lee Jae-myung administration, but we will say what needs to be said," and "We will play the role of an opposition within the ruling party." <<> Jung reportedly told those around him, "I held back and endured not being able to speak. There were many injustices." He claims that the merger with the Jo Kuk Innovation Party was promoted and announced according to the president's wishes, in coordination with the presidential office, yet the pro-Myung leadership blamed him for it and criticized him. He also argues that the abolition of prosecutorial investigation powers was a presidential campaign pledge, pursued with the consensus of the core leadership of the administration. But only the disagreement with the president was highlighted. <<> Jung said, "I lost, but our values won." To his supporters, he said, "Don't leave the party—stay to the end and protect me." Rather than accepting the election defeat gracefully and lying low, this is read as a determination to plan for the future. <<> Supreme Council member Choi Min-hee said, "I will stand with former leader Jung Cheong-rae to the end." She is vowing to remain loyal to Jung. She also said, "In a democratic party, dissenting views are natural," and "The concept of one team needs to be redefined." This means she will raise her own voice and pursue independent factionalization. <<> Representative Kim Min-seok now faces the task of coordinating between the party and the presidential office while also embracing the pro-Jung camp. If pro-Jung supreme council members like Rep. Choi Min-hee oppose Kim's line in leadership meetings, significant conflict could erupt. <<> However, it remains uncertain whether the pro-Jung camp will maintain a united front to the end. Pro-Jung lawmakers have their own nomination prospects at stake. Moreover, the pro-Myung camp's co-optation offensive will intensify. There are also predictions that some pro-Jung members could break away from Jung and cooperate with the Kim Min-seok system. <<> So, will the 'Myeong-Seok system' sail smoothly? For now, it will likely enjoy the convention bounce effect of its primary victory. The first hurdle is real estate. If they fail to present a tax revision and supply plan that the public finds convincing, the approval ratings of both the party and the presidential office could fall together. <<> The constitutional amendment and dropping prosecutorial appeals are also reefs. Pushing them too hard risks a public backlash. Whether the president's promised 2028 Honam semiconductor plant construction proceeds as planned is also critical. If the Honam semiconductor investment does not proceed as promised and hits snags, it could trigger an exodus of Honam sentiment and calls for holding the leadership accountable. <<> There is also considerable possibility that the pro-Jung camp will check Representative Kim in the supreme council. Former leader Jung Cheong-rae, author Yoo Si-min, and Kim Eo-jun could rock the Kim Min-seok system from outside. Bad news outweighs good, and risk factors are more visible than rosy forecasts. (민주당 전당대회에서 김민석 대표가 선출되면서 이재명 대통령과 김 대표가 결합한 ‘명석 체제’가 새롭게 출범했습니다. 그동안 김 대표와 경쟁하며 ‘명청 대전’을 치렀던 정청래 전 대표는 이제 야인(野人)이 됐습니다. ‘명청 갈등’의 시대는 가고 ‘명석 연대’ ‘친명 원팀’ 체제가 본격 가동된 것입니다.)

item.title: [Exclusive] Kim Yong-gwan Featured in Aug. 15 Celebration Video… Why Are His Descendants Enraged? ([단독] 8·15 경축식 영상에 나온 김용관 선생… 후손들은 왜 분노했나)
item.description:
[Exclusive] Kim Yong-gwan Featured in Aug. 15 Celebration Video… Why Are His Descendants Enraged? ([단독] 8·15 경축식 영상에 나온 김용관 선생… 후손들은 왜 분노했나)

Of the six independence activists featured in the video shown at the Aug. 15 Liberation Day ceremony, Kim Yong-gwan (1897–1967) has been confirmed not to be a "person of merit for independence" because he never received a state decoration. President Lee Jae-myung and his wife also attended the event that day. Kim Yong-gwan's bereaved family told this newspaper on the 19th: "It infuriates us that the government, which says it will expand the discovery of unhonored independence activists, refuses to recognize him as a person of merit for independence, yet politically exploits him in the Liberation Day video." <<> The ceremony video shown on the 15th at Seoul Sejong Center for the Performing Arts featured six figures: Kim Gu, Ahn Chang-ho, Lee Hoe-young, Jeong Se-kwon, Jo So-ang, and Kim Yong-gwan. Kim Yong-gwan was introduced as an activist who led industrialization under the theme "Building National Strength Through Science." However, a government official said: "In the process of producing the theme video, the Ministry of the Interior and Safety did not consult with the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, and as a result, they were apparently unaware that Kim Yong-gwan had not been selected as a person of merit for independence." <<> According to this newspaper's comprehensive reporting, the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs had rejected Kim Yong-gwan's application for recognition as a person of merit for independence three times, citing "unclear independence movement activities." When President Moon Jae-in named five "independence activists" in his Aug. 15 Liberation Day address, Kim was the only one among them who was not a recognized person of merit. At the time, public opinion called for designating Kim as a person of merit, but he ultimately never received that recognition. <<> Choi Seong-hyeon (56), the grandson-in-law of Kim Yong-gwan, told this newspaper: "There are reports that he was arrested by the Japanese police in April 1938 after giving a lecture at the Jongno YMCA hall in Seoul on the 5th Science Day, but the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs says there is no specific detention record and refuses to recognize him as a person of merit." He added, "Presenting Kim as an independence activist at an official government event is insulting and mocking his descendants." The bereaved family reportedly gave up years ago on having him recognized as a "person of merit for independence" and destroyed all related supporting documents. <<> Kim Yong-gwan studied in Japan and was a leading figure in popularizing science and technology. Believing that a scientific revival was necessary to strengthen national power, he organized the "Invention Society" in 1924 and founded "Science Joseon," Korea's first popular science magazine, in 1933. In 1934, he established "Science Day" and devoted himself to enlightenment campaigns promoting the importance of science. The Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs is known to view these activities as not being directly linked to the independence movement. The government designated Kim as a Korea Science and Technology Merit Honoree in 2020, but unlike national merit honorees, science and technology merit honorees reportedly receive no support or special treatment for their descendants. <<> Kim Geun-bae, a professor emeritus at Jeonbuk National University and current visiting professor at KAIST who specializes in modern Korean science history, said: "Even if it's hard to see a direct link to the independence movement, scientists who carried out scientific activities during the Japanese colonial period for the Korean people should be considered by the government as veterans deserving of honors equivalent to persons of merit for independence." He added, "The 'construction of a scientific Joseon' that Kim Yong-gwan and his colleagues championed at the time became linked to the 'nation-building through science' policy, which gave rise to today's Republic of Korea." (8·15 광복절 경축식 주제 영상에 등장했던 독립운동가 6명 중 김용관(1897~1967) 선생이 정부 서훈을 받지 못해 ‘독립유공자’가 아닌 것으로 확인됐다. 이날 행사엔 이재명 대통령 부부도 참석했다. 김용관 선생의 유가족은 19일 본지에 “미서훈 독립운동가 발굴을 확대하겠다는 정부가 독립유공자로 인정은 안 해주면서, 광복절 영상에서 정치적으로 이용하는 것에 분통이 터진다”고 했다.)

item.title: Ruling and Opposition Parties Hold Off on 'Yongsan Special Act Amendment'...To Be Processed After Discussions Between Ministry of Land and Seoul City (여야, ‘용산특별법 개정안’ 처리 유보…국토부·서울시 논의 후 처리키로)
item.description:
Ruling and Opposition Parties Hold Off on 'Yongsan Special Act Amendment'...To Be Processed After Discussions Between Ministry of Land and Seoul City (여야, ‘용산특별법 개정안’ 처리 유보…국토부·서울시 논의 후 처리키로)

The Democratic Party of Korea and the People Power Party announced on the 20th that they would not process the amendment to the Yongsan Park Special Act at the plenary session. The bill is centered on allowing housing supply on parts of the site within Yongsan Park. (더불어민주당과 국민의힘은 20일 본회의에서 용산공원 특별법 개정안을 처리하지 않기로 했다고 이날 밝혔다. 해당 법안은 용산공원 내 일부 부지에 주택 공급을 가능하도록 하는 내용을 골자로 한다.)

Cheon Jun-ho, the Democratic Party's chief deputy floor leader, said, "We have agreed to observe the discussions between the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the Seoul Mayor on the Yongsan Special Act, the Urban Maintenance Act, and the Urban Redevelopment Act, and to process them next week (on the 26th)." (천준호 민주당 원내수석은 “용산특별법, 도시정비법, 도시재정비법은 국토부장관과 서울시장이 논의하는 것을 지켜보고 다음주(26일)에 처리하는 것으로 의견 모았다”고 밝혔다.)

On this day, Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport Kim Yoon-deok and Seoul Mayor Oh Se-hoon were reported to have met at a location in Seoul to consult on Seoul's housing issues, including housing supply utilizing Yongsan Park. (이날 김윤덕 국토부장관과 오세훈 서울시장은 서울 모처에서 만나 용산공원을 활용한 주택 공급 등 서울 주택 문제를 협의하는 것으로 알려졌다.)

The government is reviewing a plan to utilize part of the site of Yongsan Park—a park and green area spanning 3 million square meters (approximately 907,000 pyeong)—as residential land to supply public rental housing targeting young people. Mayor Oh maintains the position that damaging the park is unacceptable, calling it "urban green space that must be passed down to future generations." (정부는 300만㎡(약 90만7000평) 규모의 공원녹지인 용산공원의 일부 부지를 주택용지로 활용해 청년층을 수요자로 하는 공공임대주택 등을 공급하는 방안을 검토 중이고, 오 시장은 “미래 세대에게 물려줘야 할 도심 녹지”라며 공원 훼손은 불가하다는 입장을 고수하고 있다.)

Meanwhile, on this day, the Democratic Party formed a 'Special Committee on Housing Supply Policy' at the Seoul city party level regarding youth housing measures, and decided to demand a youth housing supply package from the central party utilizing additional tax revenue. (한편, 이날 민주당은 서울시당 차원의 청년 주거 대책관련 ‘주택 공급 정책 특별위원회’를 구성하고, 추가 세수를 활용해 청년주택 공급 패키지를 중앙당에 요구하기로 했다.)

Kim Young-bae, chair of the Seoul city party, met with reporters after a youth housing crisis measures briefing hosted by the Seoul city party at the National Assembly Members' Hall that morning and said, "At the Seoul city party level, we will form a special committee on housing supply policy under the city party," adding, "We are planning site visits within next week." (김영배 서울시당위원장은 이날 오전 국회의원회관에서 열린 서울시당 청년 주거난 대책 간담회 후 기자들과 만나 “서울시당 차원에서 시당 산하에 주택공급 정책 특별위원회를 구성한다”며 “다음 주 중 현장 방문을 계획하고 있다”고 했다.)

Lawmaker Oh Gi-hyung will serve as chair of the special committee, with lawmaker Kim Nam-geun as secretary. Seoul city council members, district council members, and youth and housing experts are also expected to participate. (특위는 오기형 의원이 위원장을, 김남근 의원이 간사를 맡는다. 서울시의원과 자치구의원, 청년·주거 전문가 등도 참여할 예정이다.)

Furthermore, Chair Kim said, "The issue of additional tax revenue is a matter to be discussed at the party level, as Secretary General Han Jeong-ae mentioned," but also stated, "We intend to formally and actively request that the central party review a plan to supply youth housing using additional tax revenue." (또 김 위원장은 “추가 세수 문제는 한정애 사무총장도 언급하신 바와 같이 당 차원에서 논의할 문제”라면서도 “적극적으로 중앙당에 추가 세수를 활용해 청년주택을 공급하는 방안을 검토해달라고 공식적으로 요구할 생각”이라고 말했다.)

Lawmaker Oh Gi-hyung proposed a specific financial input scale of approximately 20 trillion won. Oh said, "There is tax revenue referred to as additional tax revenue," and added, "I think we should boldly invest around 20 trillion won to be used for youth housing supply." (오기형 의원은 구체적인 재정 투입 규모로 약 20조 원을 제안했다. 오 의원은 “추가 세수라고 하는 표현의 세수가 있다”며 “과감하게 20조원 정도는 들여서 청년 주거 공급에 쓰여야 하는 게 아닌가 싶다”고 말했다.)

item.title: Kim Min-seok: "Cho Hee-dae, Who Destroys the Rule of Law, Must Step Down... Ordered Nationwide Banners" (김민석 “법치파괴 조희대 물러나라... 전국에 현수막 지시”)
item.description:
Kim Min-seok: "Cho Hee-dae, Who Destroys the Rule of Law, Must Step Down... Ordered Nationwide Banners" (김민석 “법치파괴 조희대 물러나라... 전국에 현수막 지시”)

Kim Min-seok, the leader of the Democratic Party of Korea, said on the 20th, "Based on former Prime Minister Lee Hae-chan's wisdom, resolve, and transparency of putting the party first, I will carry on the legacy of a 'game maker' who builds a grand framework leading to the next general election and successive governance." (김민석 더불어민주당 대표는 20일 “이해찬 전 국무총리의 지혜와 결기, 선당후사의 투명성에 기초해 다음 총선과 연속 집권에 이르는 판을 크게 짜는 ‘판 메이커’의 뒤를 잇겠다”고 했다.)

At a visit to former Prime Minister Lee's grave at Eunhasu Park in Sejong, Representative Kim said, "Former Prime Minister Lee's politics was, first, politics of putting the public good and the party before oneself, and second, politics of building the framework." He added, "His politics was not about seeking personal advancement but about creating a framework for a large camp and forces. For a long time, I've thought that philosophically I follow in the footsteps of Kim Dae-jung, and in terms of my role in the party, I follow in the footsteps of Lee Hae-chan." (김 대표는 이날 세종 은하수공원 이 전 총리 묘역을 참배한 자리에서 “이 전 총리의 정치는 첫째는 선공후사, 선당후사의 정치고 두 번째는 판을 만드는 정치였다”며 이같이 밝혔다. 김 대표는 “본인이 뭐가 되려고 하는 정치가 아니고 큰 진영과 세력의 판을 만드는 정치를 하셨다”며 “저는 철학적으로는 김대중의 뒤를 잇고, 당에서의 역할은 이해찬의 뒤를 잇겠다는 생각을 오랫동안 해왔다”고 했다.)

Kim further stated, "I've been thinking that I should inherit the lineage of a strategist, the lineage of a game maker, following Lee Hae-chan. I will build the framework for the Democratic Party's successive governance. Not merely a victory in the general election, but I will set the structure for successive governance while looking toward a golden era for the Democratic Party spanning 20 or 30 years." (김 대표는 그러면서 “이해찬의 뒤를 이을, 일종의 전략가의 계보, 판 메이커의 계보를 이어야 되겠다는 생각을 하고 있었다”며 “민주당 연속 집권의 판을 짜겠다. 단순한 총선 승리가 아니라 20년, 30년 민주당의 황금시대를 바라보면서 연속 집권의 틀을 짜겠다”고 했다.)

Kim also said, "As the first instruction after appointing Kim Nam-jun as the publicity committee chair, I ordered that two banners be mandatorily posted nationwide. One reads, 'We will open a golden era of democracy,' and the other, 'Cho Hee-dae, who destroys the rule of law, must step down.'" (김 대표는 또 “김남준 홍보위원장 임명 후 첫 지시로 전국에 현수막 2개를 필수로 게첩하라고 지시했다”며 “하나는 ‘민주의 황금시대를 열겠습니다’, 또 하나는 ‘법치 파괴 조희대는 물러나야 한다’”라고 설명했다.)

The previous day, at his first open supreme council meeting after taking office, Kim had referred to Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae as "a delinquent student begging not to be expelled" and told him to "get out immediately." (김 대표는 전날 취임 첫 공개 최고위에선 조희대 대법원장을 향해 “퇴학을 구걸하는 불량 학생”이라며 “당장 나가라”라고 말한 바 있다.)

item.title: North Korea's Kim Yo-jong Demands "Halt" to US-South Korea Drills, Raising Bar for Dialogue (北 김여정, 韓美훈련 축소에 “중단” 요구… 대화 문턱 높여)
item.description:
North Korea's Kim Yo-jong Demands "Halt" to US-South Korea Drills, Raising Bar for Dialogue (北 김여정, 韓美훈련 축소에 “중단” 요구… 대화 문턱 높여)

In response to US President Donald Trump's repeated offers of dialogue with North Korea, accompanied by his directive to downsize US-South Korea military exercises, Pyongyang has countered by demanding a halt to the drills, turning the ball back to Washington. Analysts interpret this as North Korea raising the threshold and the stakes for dialogue amid Trump's successive public overtures. Both Washington and Pyongyang are signaling the possibility of resuming talks, emphasizing that "relations between the leaders are good," yet neither side has made any mention of denuclearization. (한미군사훈련 축소를 지시한 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령의 잇따른 대북 대화 제의에 북한은 훈련 중단 등을 요구하며 공을 미국으로 넘겼다. 북한이 트럼프의 잇따른 공개 대화 제의에 대화 문턱과 몸값 높이기에 들어갔다는 분석이다. 미·북 양국 모두 “정상 간 관계는 좋다”는 점을 앞세워 대화 재개 가능성을 열어 둔 메시지를 발신하고 있으나 비핵화에 대한 언급은 어느 쪽도 하지 않고 있다.)

◆North Korea Raises Dialogue Threshold from Downsizing to Halting US-South Korea Drills, Demanding Withdrawal of "Hostile Policy" (◆한미 군사훈련 축소→중단, “대북 적대정책” 철회 등 대화 문턱 높인 北)

North Korea experts analyzed on the 20th that Kim Yo-jong, vice department director of the Workers' Party, in her statement on "positions on major international issues" issued through the Korean Central News Agency the previous day, mentioned that "the reduction or shortening of individual exercises does not change the fact that joint military exercises between the US and South Korea have been continuously conducted and are still ongoing," effectively setting the condition for dialogue as a halt to the US-South Korea military drills, not merely a reduction. (북한 전문가들은 20일 전날 김여정 노동당 부장이 조선중앙통신을 통해 발표한 ‘주요국 문제들에 대한 입장’에서 “개별적 훈련의 축소나 단축이 아니라 현재까지 미·한 사이의 합동 군사연습이 지속적으로 진행되어 오고 있고 지금도 진행 중에 있다”고 언급한 데 대해 한미군사훈련 축소가 아닌 중단을 대화 조건으로 제시한 것이라고 분석했다.)

()

Kim Yo-jong stated that although the Ulchi Freedom Shield (UFS) exercise, which began on the 17th, was significantly downsized following President Trump's directive, she "does not consider it worthy of evaluation and has no interest in it whatsoever." She added, "The reduction in scale or duration does not change the nature of these provocative and aggressive military exercises," and "the downsized exercise this time has been more than sufficiently substituted by previous joint drills." Kim Yo-jong went further, warning, "If the US side calculates to tout its recent measure as some sort of 'act of goodwill,' it will not get the answer it wants." (김여정은 지난 17일부터 시작한 ‘을지 자유의 방패(UFS)’ 훈련이 트럼프 대통령 지시에 따라 대폭 축소됐으나 “그에 대해 평할 가치도 없다고 보며 전혀 흥미를 느끼지 않는다”고 했다. 김여정은 “훈련의 규모나 기일이 줄어든다고 해서 도발적, 공격적 성격의 군사연습의 본질이 달라지는 것이 아니다”며 “이번에 축소되었다는 연습 과정이 이미 전에 진행된 연합 훈련들에 의해 충분히 대체되고도 남는다”고 했다. 김여정은 더 나아가 “미국 측이 이번에 취한 자기들의 조치를 그 무슨 ‘선의의 조치’로 선전해보려고 타산한다면 원하는 답이 나오지 않을 것”이라고 했다.)

Hong Min, senior research fellow at the Korea Institute for National Unification, said, "By targeting the 'continuity' itself, not just the scale or duration of the drills, they have effectively set the demand level from 'reduction' to 'halt,'" adding, "Rather than a one-off gesture of goodwill, they are presenting substantive confidence-building measures and a fundamental change in hostile attitudes as the threshold for dialogue." Yang Moo-jin, chair professor at the University of North Korean Studies, also said, "It's an assertion that downsizing the US-South Korea joint exercises is not enough; the US must abolish its hostile policy," and noted, "Given that she dismissed suspicions of additional Russian troop deployments and referenced Japan's recent military moves and our pursuit of nuclear-powered submarines, this is an attempt to raise the threshold for US-North Korea dialogue by voicing objections on all security issues relevant to them." (홍민 통일연구원 선임연구위원은 “훈련의 규모나 기간이 아닌 ‘지속성’ 자체를 문제 삼아 요구 수준을 (훈련) 축소에서 사실상 ‘중단’으로 설정한 것”이라며 “일회성 선의가 아니라 실질적 신뢰구축 조치, 적대성에 대한 근본적 태도 변화를 대화의 문턱으로 제시한 것”이라고 했다. 양무진 북한대학원대학교 석좌교수도 “한미연합훈련 축소 갖고는 안 되고 미국의 적대 정책을 철폐하라는 주장”이라며 “러시아 추가 파병 의혹을 일축하고 최근 일본의 군사 동향과 우리의 핵잠 개발 추진 등을 언급한 점으로 미뤄 자신들과 유관한 모든 안보 이슈에 대한 항변을 통해 북미 대화의 문턱을 높이려는 것”이라고 했다.)

◆Late-Night Statement Issued on Day of Wang Yi's Visit to South Korea… "Making Clear There's No Compromise on Military Buildup Despite Good Relations with Trump" (◆왕이 방한일에 심야 입장 발표… “트럼프와 관계 좋지만 군사력 강화 타협 없다는 점 분명히”)

Kim Yo-jong's late-night statement came on the same day that China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi visited South Korea for the South Korea-China foreign ministerial meeting. Professor Yang Moo-jin said, "Timing it to coincide with the South Korea-China foreign ministerial meeting implies an intention to showcase leadership on Korean Peninsula issues," adding, "The emergency statement also appears aimed at curbing premature expectations for US-North Korea dialogue." (김여정의 한밤중 입장 발표는 중국의 왕이 외교부장 방한으로 한·중 외교 장관 회담이 열린 날 이뤄졌다. 양무진 교수는 “시점상 한·중 외교 장관 회담에 맞춤으로서 한반도 문제의 주도권 과시를 내포하고 있는 것”이라며 “긴급 입장 발표를 통해 북미 대화에 섣부른 기대감을 차단하는 의도도 있어 보인다”고 했다.)

Kim Yo-jong chose the format of a "statement on positions on major international issues" rather than a "message targeting the US" alone. In the order of the statement, she reaffirmed existing positions on the Russia-Ukraine war situation, the Korean Peninsula situation, and the Middle East, Europe, and Asia-Pacific situations, then highlighted the alliance with Russia as "infinitely responsible," criticized Japan's rearmament threats, and only then addressed Trump's downsizing of military exercises. Kim Yo-jong said, "We have already stated several times that our state leader (Kim Jong-un) has good personal memories and feelings toward Trump," and "the relationship between the two leaders is excellent." Nevertheless, she said, "Despite that, the US hostile policy toward North Korea has not changed, and the US and its followers are intensively conducting hostile military activities against North Korea at this very moment." Kim Yo-jong added, "We remind that regardless of the excellent relationship between the leaders of the two countries, the sovereign exercises we take to counter forces threatening our national security are very commonsensical, accurate, and necessary." This signals a continuation of the existing nuclear force-building line. Im Eul-chul, professor at Kyungnam University's Institute for Far Eastern Studies, said, "While acknowledging the 'excellent personal relationship' between Kim Jong-un and Trump, she made clear the position toward the US that there will never be a compromise on national security or military buildup due to personal ties." (김여정은 미국을 단독 상대로 설정한 ‘대미 담화’가 아닌 ‘주요국 문제들에 대한 입장 발표’ 형식을 선택했다. 발표 순서를 보면 러시아·우크라이나 전쟁 국면과 한반도 정세, 중동·유럽 및 아시아·태평양 정세에 대한 기존 입장을 재확인한 뒤 러시아와의 동맹 관계에 대해 “무한히 책임적”이라며 부각하고 일본의 재군사 위협을 비난한 뒤에야 트럼프의 군사훈련 축소에 대한 입장을 언급했다. 김여정은 “우리 국가수반(김정은)이 트럼프에 대하여 개인적으로 좋은 추억과 감정을 가지고 있다는데 대해서는 이미 여러 차례 밝힌 바 있다”며 “두 지도자의 관계는 의견 훌륭하다”고 했다. 그러면서도 “그럼에도 불구하고 미국의 대조선 적대시 정책은 변하지 않아 왔고 미국과 그 추종 무리들은 오늘 현재 이 순간도 적대적인 대조선(북한) 군사 활동을 맹렬히 벌리고 있다”고 했다. 김여정은 “조미(북미) 두 나라 지도자들 사이의 훌륭한 관계와는 무관하게 우리가 자국의 안전을 위협하는 세력들을 견제하기 위한 취해 나가는 주권적 행사들은 매우 상식적이고 적중하며 필수적인 것으로 된다는 것을 상기시킨다”고 했다. 기존의 핵 무력 강화 노선을 그대로 유지하겠다는 얘기다. 임을출 경남대 극동문제연구소 교수는 “김정은과 트럼프 간 ‘훌륭한 개인적 관계’는 인정하지만 개인적 친분 때문에 국가 안보 및 군사력 강화를 타협하는 일은 절대 없다는 명확한 대미 입장을 밝힌 것”이라고 했다.)

◆South Korean Government: "We Hope North Korea Joins in President Trump's Bold Decision" (◆정부 “트럼프 대통령의 통 큰 결단에 북측도 동참하기를”)

In response to Kim Yo-jong's statement from the previous day, the Ministry of Unification said on that day, "What must come first is ending the war on the Korean Peninsula and building a peace regime where there is no need for the two sides to fight each other." (통일부는 이날 김여정의 전날 입장 발표에 대해 “무엇보다 우선돼야 할 것은 한반도에서 전쟁을 끝내고 서로 싸울 필요가 없는 평화 체제를 만드는 것”이라는 입장을 냈다.)

The ministry stated, "President Trump's downsizing of the US-South Korea joint exercises is a decision to begin dialogue for building a peace regime on the Korean Peninsula," adding, "We hope North Korea will join in this opportunity so that President Trump's bold decision can lead to a history of peace, including the resumption of US-North Korea summit talks within this year and the establishment of a stable peace regime on the Korean Peninsula." The ministry also said, "The government will make every effort as a pacesetter and a party to peace on the Korean Peninsula so that the opportunity for peace created by President Trump as a peacemaker can yield tangible results." (통일부는 “트럼프 대통령의 한미연합연습 축소는 한반도에서 평화 체제 구축을 위한 대화를 시작하려는 결단”이라며 “트럼프 대통령의 통 큰 결단이 금년 내 미·북 정상 간 대화 재개와 한반도의 안정적 평화 체제 구축이라는 평화의 역사로 이어질 수 있도록, 북측도 이 기회에 동참하기를 기대한다”고 했다. 통일부는 “정부는 트럼프 대통령이 피스메이커로서 만든 평화의 기회가 실질적인 성과로 이어질 수 있도록 페이스메이커이자 한반도 평화의 당사자로서 모든 노력을 다할 것”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Ahn Gyu-baek: "North Korea Has 80–120 Nuclear Weapons... We Should Not Accept U.S. Tactical Nukes" (안규백 “北 핵무기 80~120개... 美전술핵 받아들이면 안된다”)
item.description:
Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-baek said on the 20th regarding the status of North Korea's nuclear weapons: "We generally estimate around 80 to 120, but giving an exact figure is quite limited." (안규백 국방부 장관은 20일 북한의 핵무기 보유 현황에 대해 “우리가 보통은 80∼120개 정도로 보는데 정확한 수치를 말하는 것은 상당히 제한적”이라고 했다.)

Minister Ahn made these remarks while attending the National Assembly's National Defense Committee, responding to a question from People Power Party lawmaker Seong Il-jong asking for the government's assessment of North Korea's nuclear development status. (안 장관은 이날 국회 국방위원회에 출석해 북한의 핵 개발 현황에 대한 정부 평가를 묻는 국민의힘 성일종 의원 질의에 이렇게 답했다.)

Regarding U.S. President Donald Trump specifying North Korea's nuclear weapons as "57," Minister Ahn said, "The numbers seem to differ somewhat." The Ministry of National Defense stated, "The number of North Korean nuclear weapons Minister Ahn mentioned that day refers to an estimate by a domestic research institute." (안 장관은 도널드 트럼프 미국 대통령이 북한 핵무기를 ‘57개’로 특정한 것과 관련해 “약간 숫자는 상이한 것 같다”고 했다. 국방부는 “안 장관이 이날 언급한 북한 핵무기 수량은 국내 연구기관이 추정한 수량을 언급한 것”이라고 했다.)

President Trump, in a meeting with reporters at the White House, said he was "getting along very well" with North Korean State Affairs Commission Chairman Kim Jong-un, adding, "He has 57 very powerful nuclear weapons." It is highly unusual for a U.S. president to specifically cite a figure related to North Korea's nuclear arsenal. Details on North Korea's nuclear capabilities are classified information between South Korea and the United States. (트럼프 대통령은 백악관에서 취재진과 만난 자리에서 김정은 북한 국무위원장과 “잘 지내고 있다”며 “그는 57개의 매우 강력한 핵무기를 갖고 있다”고 했다. 미국 대통령이 북한의 핵무기 관련 수치를 구체적으로 특정한 건 상당히 이례적인 일이다. 북한 핵 능력과 관련한 세부 내용은 한미 양국의 기밀 사안이다.)

When asked whether he acknowledged that North Korea possesses nuclear weapons, Minister Ahn said, "That cannot be officially acknowledged." To a question asking whether President Trump's specific mention of 57 nuclear weapons constituted recognition of North Korea's nuclear arsenal, he said, "It seems inappropriate for the South Korean defense minister to comment on that." Minister Ahn added, "We cannot develop nuclear weapons. We also should not accept the deployment of U.S. tactical nuclear weapons, and we are consistently pursuing a policy of receiving a firm commitment to the U.S. nuclear umbrella." (안 장관은 북한이 핵을 갖고 있는 것은 인정하느냐는 질문에는 “그것은 공식적으로 인정할 수 없다”고 했다. 핵무기 숫자를 트럼프 대통령이 57개라고 구체적으로 거론한 것은 북한의 핵무기 보유를 인정한 것 아니냐는 질문에는 “한국 국방장관이 거기에 대해 논평한다는 건 적절치 않은 것 같다”고 했다. 안 장관은 “우리는 핵을 개발할 수 없다”며 “미국의 전술핵(배치)도 우리가 받아들이면 안 된다”면서 “미국의 핵우산을 확실히 제공받는 정책으로 우리가 일관되게 나가고 있는 것”이라고 했다.)

Minister Ahn also responded to Reform Party lawmaker Cheon Ha-ram, who demanded the disclosure of military service records related to allegations of desertion, saying, "I have no shame before heaven" and "It is completely contrary to the facts." He added, "If there were any such desertion, then I am the son of lawmaker Han Ki-ho," and "After I leave public office, I intend to settle this matter through legal and administrative procedures." (안 장관은 이날 탈영 의혹 관련 병적기록부 공개를 요구하는 개혁신당 천하람 의원에게 “하늘을 우러러 한 점 부끄러움이 없다”며 “완전 사실과 다른 내용”이라고 했다. 그러면서 “만약 탈영 이런 부분이 있다면 제가 한기호 의원 아들”이라며 “제가 공직을 그만둔 뒤 이런 부분에 대해 법적, 행정적 절차를 가지고 마무리할 생각”이라고 했다.)
